title: Evidence-led market portrait for model-fit and procurement hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce an evidence-backed market portrait that translates model landscape signals into procurement-ready hooks for sales and finance. The output will be: (1) a short executive deck (10 slides) that highlights supplier capability clusters, latency/cost buckets, and high-risk substitution vectors for enterprise customers; (2) a prioritized supplier scorecard (CSV + rubric) for use by procurement and solutions; (3) a small ruleset (prototype boolean rules + examples) that surfaces triggers when a model supply signal should escalate to SRE/Legal/Sales.

Scope and questions we will answer: Which open and hosted model families are within a 15% perf/cost envelope for common enterprise workloads (chat-short, embeddings-1k, RAG)? Which models have quantization/edge variants that materially reduce unit cost while preserving quality? What regional availability constraints (APAC/EU) create realistic fallback gaps? What are the top 6 procurement hooks (contract asks, pricing guardrails, SLA knobs, fallback entitlements, private deployment requirements, quantization acceptance language) that will reduce renewal friction?

Data sources and signals: internal telemetry (token latency, per-route model selection) dashboards, recent procurement CSM notes (Drive/Doc link below), open-model release logs, community benchmarks, GitHub issues for major model runtimes, cloud region capacity reports, SRE incident postmortems (related to model outages).

Deliverables: 
- Executive deck (PDF) with 3-slide narrative: supply landscape, friction map, recommended procurement hooks.
- Supplier scorecard CSV with columns: model_family, typical_latency_p50_ms, cost_token_usd_est, quant_variant_available, regional_availability, integration_effort_est (1-5), estimated_switch_cost.
- Rulebook prototype (markdown) with 6 trigger rules and example inputs for Signal-Ingestion pipeline.
- Short README and a Canonical Notebook (Colab) that shows the microbench methodology used to compare 3 representative workloads.

Approach: 1) quick data pull and narrow microbench for 5 representative prompts per workload; 2) normalize latency and cost to a single reference hardware and context length; 3) map quant/variant availability and documented compatibility quirks; 4) interview 4 customer-facing reps (sales, SRE, procurement, solutions) for real-world pain points; 5) synthesize procurement hooks prioritized by expected renewal friction reduction.

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha, Liam), Solutions (Marisol Vega), SRE (Daniel Kim), Procurement lead (Claire N'guyen), Sales Engineering (Owen Park).

Success metrics: Deck accepted by Head of Product and shared with Sales; scorecard validated against 3 active deals; prototype rulebook gets initial ingestion in Signal Pipeline staging.

Constraints / trade-offs: This is a 3-week lightweight probe, not an exhaustive landscape study. We will trade absolute coverage for repeatable signals and quick operationalization. Quantization accuracy evaluation will use proxy prompts and limited domain tests — flag as further work if shown high variance.

Acceptance criteria: deck + scorecard + rulebook + notebook committed to Drive and referenced in the procurement playbook; at least 2 follow-up tasks created for implementation (e.g., Signal pipeline mapping, procurement contract wording drafts).

References/links: Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PL/pages/Market+Portrait+PM-5050505 (draft); Drive deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/market-portrait-pm-5050505 (placeholder); Notebook: https://colab.research.google.com/drive/microbench-pm-5050505 (prototype); Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood/projects/telemetry/model-supply (internal).
